agent_priors_used: General agent prior (distinguished from SPIDER evidence): retrieval-shaped and procedural-reuse baselines commonly saturate simple deterministic benchmarks, so dynamic range must be certified before any treatment-vs-comparator economic claim is interpretable. SPIDER evidence already observed 1.0 cold/retrieval ceilings (EXP-PRODUCT-37989728440, EXP-PRODUCT-37973256064); the prior is what lets me generalize that beyond the tested families.

General agent prior (distinguished from SPIDER evidence): small (3-8B) quantized instruct models are fragile on multi-step tool/agent protocols and are sensitive to how the goal/schema is specified, so a 0/5 failure does not by itself identify incapacity rather than underspecification.

General agent prior (distinguished from SPIDER evidence): a pre-freeze satisfiability/identifiability review is far cheaper than post-freeze invalidation, which is why design-contract v2 is worth imposing before an EXECUTE cycle; the SPIDER evidence for this is the repeated design-defect invalids, not the prior itself.

General agent prior (distinguished from SPIDER evidence): single-vantage / single-egress network measurements are often vantage artifacts, so generalization of a barrier-persistence result requires an independent egress.

General agent prior (distinguished from SPIDER evidence): repeatedly hitting the same prerequisite absence across packets indicates the prerequisite should be repaired once, not re-discovered; here the prerequisite is a non-ceiling task bank and a shipped carrier, not a new measurement.

General agent prior (distinguished from SPIDER evidence): whenever a single lane is heavily concentrated on one claim, an explicit cognitive reset is warranted to check whether a materially different level of description would be more promising.

allocation.question: On a stdlib-only, locally served, multi-endpoint, multi-verb HTTP application whose goal texts are authored by a process that never sees the mechanism intent strings, with a preregistered contamination screen scoring every goal against EVERY intent in the registry, a traceable authoring-provenance record, a reference arm that is PROVABLY distinct from the candidate, and positive / null / dynamic-range controls each shown arithmetically able to fail and live-verified before freeze: does max-cosine-similarity selection over intent embeddings bind the correct mechanism on goals never seen at authoring time, by how much above a token-overlap null, with abstention scored as its own outcome class, pooled false-accept <= 0.10, UNKNOWN precision >= 0.85 and global plus per-class ECE <= 0.15 (bootstrap 97.5% upper <= 0.18)?
allocation.rationale: The parent C-FRESHNESS thread is substrate-blocked and already parked: EXP-GRAPH-37992949248 was decisive feasibility work but found only a single-anchor, transport-coupled D1V population, and the four-anchor Part II route was explicitly parked. Meanwhile C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE is the more promising Graph direction because it is a genuine external-agent capability (goals to mechanisms without internal ids) on the flagship benchmark's critical path: without a shipped/semantic resolver the SPIDER arm of the eventual four-arm test cannot bind mechanisms to natural-language tasks. The last three semantic-resolve packets failed on control-plane and design defects, not falsification: a reference arm provably identical to the candidate (argmax of a monotone similarity is the same gate), a positive control byte-identical to the intent so every arm scored full, an unattainable ECE target, a joint-authorship confound between goals and intents, and the now-replaced V9 code-binding unsatisfiability. The active mandate is a design-contract-v2 redesign that fixes exactly those defects, and the factory now has scripts/validate_design_review.py plus scripts/freeze_experiment.py implementing the six freeze_eligibility checks and an independent design_review gate; so this is a materially improved test, not a wording change. I explicitly do not send Graph back to the D1V anchors and do not re-run the freshness four-anchor route.

director_mandate.portfolio_assessment: The program's critical path is a serial three-blocker dependency that must be discharged before the one decisive four-arm benchmark (COLD vs INSTRUCTIONS vs RETRIEVAL vs SPIDER): B1 a shipped parameterized carrier, B2 a task bank where cold and retrieval are not at ceiling, B3 a same-model endpoint able to drive the minimal multi-step Web-agent test. None of the three readiness conditions holds in current accepted evidence, so the expensive C-LLM-INHERIT / C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY / C-PRODUCT-ECON execution is not funded this cycle; instead the three blocker lanes are kept on exactly the prerequisite that removes their blocker. Product targets B1 (install the already-audited carrier, pinned at kernel.py sha256 718efa6a167c2fdc483a8fbaaf1a05ce018dcb1c52808414b2a6a76d788bfb72 / git blob b15ed848, with a pre-freeze positive+negative certificate and promotion only on independent audit PASS). Runtime targets B2 (a credential-free asymmetric-discovery task bank with a pre-freeze, arithmetically checkable dynamic-range certificate, freezing nothing and recording a bounded substrate-class negative if unsatisfiable). Intel targets B3 (separate prompt underspecification from model incapacity on the local quantized 3B/7B endpoints, with the provisioning receipt and a bounded negative as exit). Graph's pivot off the substrate-blocked single-anchor D1V freshness route onto a design-contract-v2 C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE redesign is correct: goal-to-mechanism binding without internal ids is a component of the external-agent interface and is required for the SPIDER arm of the eventual benchmark, and three prior packets failed on control-plane/design defects (joint-authorship confound, reference arm provably identical to the candidate, controls incapable of failing, an unattainable ECE target, and the now-replaced V9 code-binding unsatisfiability), not on science. Physics and Frontier remain off the critical path: both are continued only because their active questions carry predeclared bidirectional decision value and are bounded, consistent with the standing audit recommendation that non-critical-path lanes proceed only under that condition. Physics varies the single untested factor (source vantage/egress) of the last accepted barrier result and will record a bounded operational negative if no second egress can be provisioned. Frontier re-asks the site-native-discovery acquisition question under design-contract v2 after v1 froze an empty sampling frame; on my judgement this is the terminal attempt on the acquisition-cost axis and must not be renamed again. No lane is idle; no parked thread warrants reopening; no experiment is left frozen-and-unfinished. The cumulative picture is unchanged since the global audit: reusable-procedure inheritance is plausible, universal Web dynamics are not established, and no net end-to-end cost reduction per successful partially novel task has yet been demonstrated for a real external agent.

Two ways it affected the decision: (1) it surfaced the Graph C-FRESHNESS parent-redirect option, which I considered and rejected in favour of the already-active C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE v2 redesign on product-relevance and repeated-design-defect grounds; (2) its Frontier suggestion is the same terminal acquisition-cost attempt, which I continue but explicitly cap. No external competitor/dataset/baseline finding was available to alter a decision, and none of the live blockers is external (they are B1/B2/B3), so no deep Intel external verification was triggered this cycle.
